## Summary

This notebook demonstrates how to download data from the 'Cleaned CIMIS' table which is hosted on [PGFarm](https://pgfarm.library.ucdavis.edu/). These data are available from a public PostgresSQL database, and do not require a login or API key.

::: {.callout-tip title="Other Ways to Download the Data"}
The 'Cleaned CIMIS' data is in a standard PostgresSQL database, which can be accessed through several programming languages and front ends, including Python, psql, JavaScript, etc. For further details, see the [Access Examples](https://pgfarm.library.ucdavis.edu/db/uc-anr/tree-chill) on PGFarm.
:::

You can also view a snapshot of the amount of cleaned CIMIS data on the [PG Farm Cleaned CIMIS Data Dashboard](https://ucanr.app/cleancimis_stats).

::: {.callout-note title="Other Tasks"}

This notebook does **not** have sample code to predict bark temperature from ambient conditions for cherry trees, nor compute chill portions based on the predicted bark temperature. For those tasks, you'll need to install the [`cherrychill`](https://github.com/ucanr-igis/cherrychill) R package (which is not public, contact Andy for details).

This notebook also does not have the code to download and clean raw CIMIS data. This is done automatically on a nightly basis.

:::

## Setup

First, load the libraries we're going to need below.

```{r message=FALSE}
library(DBI)
library(RPostgres)
library(glue)
library(cli)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Load Convenience Functions 

To help you download the data, there are two convenience functions available on Github: [`cleancimis_qry()`](https://github.com/UCANR-IGIS/sketchbook/blob/main/cleancimis_qry.R) and [`cleancimis_stn()`](https://github.com/UCANR-IGIS/sketchbook/blob/main/cleancimis_stn.R): 

```{r}
source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/UCANR-IGIS/sketchbook/refs/heads/main/cleancimis_qry.R")
source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/UCANR-IGIS/sketchbook/refs/heads/main/cleancimis_stn.R")
```

## Get the Stations

Grab the list of stations that are saved in the database:

```{r}
cimis_stn_tbl <- cleancimis_stn()
```

View the list of stations:

```{r}
cimis_stn_tbl$station_n
```

## Download Data for Station #105

To download data for a single station, let's first take a look at the arguments we can use with `cleancimis_qry()`:

```{r}
args(cleancimis_qry)
```

Now we're ready to download data for station #105:

```{r}
## Download data for one station
cimis_data_tbl <- cleancimis_qry(station_n = 105)

head(cimis_data_tbl)
```

View the range of dates for this station:

```{r}
range(cimis_data_tbl$date_time)
```

::: {.callout-note title="A Gap in the Data"}
Note that CIMIS changed their API in June 2026, and stopped supporting the old API in mid-July. Hence there is a break in the data from mid-July onward.

We are working on updating the daily download script to use the new API. Once that is done, we'll be able to back fill the missing data.

:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Getting Data for Multiple Stations"}
Note if you want to download data for multiple stations simultaneously, you can pass a vector of integers to `station_n`. Example:

`cimis_data_tbl <- cleancimis_qry(station_n = c(80, 105))`

:::

## Download Data for a Date Range

Suppose we wanted to download data for just January 2026. Fortunately, `cleancimis_qry()` has two optional arguments we can use to ask for data for a specific time period.

First we need to create objects for the start and end time:

```{r}
jan01_dt <- lubridate::ymd_hm("2026/01/01 00:00", tz = "America/Los_Angeles")
jan31_dt <- lubridate::ymd_hm("2026/01/31 23:59", tz = "America/Los_Angeles")
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Don't Forget the Time!"}
CIMIS weather variables are recorded **hourly**. Therefore when querying the data you must always pass date-time values, even if you are  interested in filtering by date. When constructing time values, remember that every day starts at midnight (`00:00`) and ends at 11:59pm (`23:59`). 
Example:

`end_dt <- lubridate::ymd_hm("2026/01/31 23:59", tz = "America/Los_Angeles")`

:::

Now we are ready to get the data for this month:

```{r}
stn105_jan26_tbl <- cleancimis_qry(start_dt = jan01_dt, end_dt = jan31_dt, station_n = 105)

head(stn105_jan26_tbl)
tail(stn105_jan26_tbl)
```

\

To verify the data are complete, we can plot air temperature:

```{r}
ggplot(stn105_jan26_tbl, aes(x = date_time, y = st_t_air_C)) +
  geom_line()
```

## What Next?

You can use `cleancimis_qry()` to query the cleaned CIMIS data by station and/or date range. What you get back is a tibble (data frame).

Next, you can use any of the usual methods from the tidyverse to further filter the data, group rows, compute summaries, etc. You can also export it to csv or other format using `readr` or similiar packages.
